definition: Artisto is a video processing application with art and movie effects filters based on neural network algorithms created in 2016 by Mail.ru Group machine learning specialists.
details: At the moment the application can process videos up to 10 seconds long and offers users 21 filters, including those based on the works of famous artists (e.g. Blue Dream — Pablo Picasso), theme-based (Rio-2016 — related to the 2016 Summer Olympics in Rio de Janeiro) and others. The app works with both pre-recorded videos and videos recorded with the application.

explainer.lead: Artisto is a video-effects application created in 2016 by machine-learning specialists at Mail.ru Group. It uses neural-network algorithms to give short clips artistic or cinematic looks, making this kind of visual transformation accessible through a filter-based app.

tiers.eli5: Artisto is like a costume box for a short video: you choose a costume, and the app changes how the whole clip looks. Some costumes are inspired by famous paintings, while others follow a theme such as the Rio 2016 Olympics. You can use a video you already recorded or make one inside the app.
tiers.practitioner: Artisto is an end-user video-processing application, with filter selection as the main setting. Its described workflow supports pre-recorded or in-app recordings up to 10 seconds long and offers 21 filters. Longer videos fall outside that limit, and the available information does not describe an API, model export, or custom-filter controls.
tiers.paperLevel: Artisto can be described as y = F_f(x), where x is a pre-recorded or in-app video of at most 10 seconds, f is one of 21 art, movie, or theme filters, and F_f is video processing based on neural-network algorithms. The filter set includes learned styles associated with particular artists or themes; no specific network architecture, training procedure, or originating paper is identified.

explainer.example: A user selects an eight-second pre-recorded clip and applies Blue Dream. Artisto processes the clip with a filter based on Pablo Picasso's works, returning a short video with that artistic look.

explainer.intuition: The app treats a visual style as something that can be applied to a video, much like choosing a filter for a photo. Instead of manually redrawing each frame, the user selects a clip and lets neural-network-based processing produce the styled result.
howItWorks: Record a video in Artisto or choose a pre-recorded clip.
Keep the input within the application's 10-second limit.
Choose one of 21 artistic, cinematic, or themed filters.
The app processes the clip with neural-network algorithms and produces a styled video.
explainer.whyItMatters: Artisto packages neural-network-based video styling into a simple consumer workflow. Its short clips and ready-made filters let users create artistic or themed videos without designing an effect themselves.
misconceptions: It processes videos, not just still photographs.
A Picasso-based filter creates an effect inspired by his works, not an authentic Picasso artwork.
The described 10-second limit means it is not intended for processing full-length videos.
